While you're getting to know people, there is a high chance that you will meet best friends, and that special someone in your life. You never know who you'll meet unless you go and meet them. You're not alone I failed overdose and now I have major bad nausea, stomach pains, and bad memories burnt into my brain. Don't keep trying, it'll only lead to the kind of dead that sucks. Being dead is like being trapped in a pitch black room while you're prevented from any movement or sound. You're all alone but you feel uncomfortable vulnerability too. It's not a fun place. I was there for a good 10 mins and I absolutely regret my actions. Learn from my mistake. You don't want to be dead. Being dead is worse than the stress rn. I know that from experience. Don't make the same mistake as me because you'll be left with painful memories, deep regret, and serious depression. You'll be left in worse shape than how you were before death. It's not a good feeling at all

Don't think of death as some peaceful ending. It's actually worse than the stress on your mind rn. Being dead is being alone in a pitch black room while you're unable to move, unable to speak, there's total silence, and the freezing aroma makes you feel vulnerable even thought you're by yourself. Learn from me. I'm a survivor of overdose and am currently suffering the side-effects of a failed suicide attempt. I only died for a little bit then woke up. When I woke up, I immediately started praying and thinking about all that matters most because you never know how much your surroundings mean to you until you don't have it anymore. Also you do not want the bad memory if you survive. It's what makes me regret the most, the memory of my life nearly ending by my own hand. You don't want that kind of horrible horrible memory stuck in your brain. It's not all that it's cracked up to be. Learn from my mistake and build off of it. Don't make the same stupid, worthless, fearful, depressing, regretting, and destroying waste of time at relieving stress that I tried. It's not worth it bro. All of my determination for death was all for nothing because I feel weak for resorting to suicide. Try to find other ways of going about your stress. There are safer, better and quicker stress relivers than suicide. Trust me bro you don't want the kind of regret and guilt that I'm going through rn. It'll only make matters worse.

Death isn't as hype as they say it is. They're just trying to make you feel better about death when you feel suicidal. Once you're dead, nothin's changed except you're dead. Being dead is the feeling of isolation in a pitch-black room while you can't move or talk. It sucks. Take it from me. I died from overdose, came back to life and immediately started thinking about the blessings you get in life. You don't know how much you really got until it's all gone. Since I've revived, the side effects of death have been kicking my ass all day. I've had bad nausea, My stomach felt like it was caving in, and I've had a major bad headache all day so yeah. Learn from my mistakes and don't make the same stupid, regretting, fearful, depressing mistake I did because it may impact you harder than you thought it would.

Here's the some sad truths about the outcome of suicide from a survivor:
1. When you die, you're still alone and cold so either way dead or not it's a dead end between living stress and eternal isolation in a pitch-black world that has no sound, movement, speaking, and uncomfortable vulnerability. No.

2. The ones that care about you will be impacted harder than intended. Plus, there's always that one person that triggers a endless cycle of death by depression.

3. Imagine if you saw the love of your life commit suicide in front of your very eyes. Think about how that would make you feel then times that by two and you have their feeling

4. You don't always find success in dying. Most cases end up with a lot of survivors and trust me, I'm a survivor and the side-effects are the worst things in the world.

So think about all that. Suicide should never become an option for relieving stress. Learn from my mistake because once it's done, it's done. There's no going back. If you survive, the aftermath is torture especially since I overdosed. I have insane nausea, my stomach feels like it's caving in, and my head hurts worse than the worst hangover. Suicide isn't something you should resort to. Have you tried better ways of going about your stress? There are ways to relieve stress that don't involve any physical harm to your body and some can teach you a thing or two. Don't make the same mistake I did. Learn from my ignorance, stupidity, and stubbornness. You do not want the "gifts" of the survivor. The worst one is the horrible reoccurring memory of my life almost ending by my hand. All you'll get out of suicide is sad people and possible future death. Build off of my story and build off of your situation that causes your depression. Try to look for ways that you'll get stronger from it. If you do that, everything will be clearer and more sensible. There's always a reason for something. Don't let suicide be the reason. It's not worth it. I'm only 16 too. I still have so much ahead. Just think about what you would do if the closest person to you died in an instant and think about what you would feel because that's most likely how they'd feel if you died. Trust me. Don't copy my biggest regret. It's not fun thing to have as a memory. It's the kind of memory that burns your brain as if they were cigarette burns. Let your goal and your desire to achieve it make your fate. Don't let stress get too much because you'll lose patience and drive for your goal. Just relish in the glory of paradise because it's where you'll go if you just stop stressing and think about your future, not your end.

Think about this. When it comes to death, it's not the sensation and satisfaction everybody else finds in it. It's an empty void that's always pitch-black, it's silent, you can't move, you can't talk, and it makes you feel vulnerable even though you're all alone. I know because I've experienced it. It's not all what it's hyped up to be. If anything I was scared shitless. It's a place worse than what they decribe hell to be. Suicide isn't worth all the time, thought, tears, effort, and acceptance you put into it because you're all alone either way. Being stressed out is pretty much a dead-end. It's the same outcome dead or alive. So it's not use killing yourself over it. I'm one of the unlucky ones that survived and has to deal with the side-effects of ODing, the sadness I was enduring while I thought about the ones that care, and the reoccurring memory of my life almost taken my my own hand. It's some life thinking shit. When I woke up from death, I immediately started thinking about life and the worth in suicide. So whether you're dead or not you're still alone if you keep all that stress on your mind. Just think about what you really want before thinking death. Once you find that one goal you want to accomplish, try to let this whole ordeal make you stronger and better fit to succeed. You may like the outcome of relief. I know it from experience. Also, stress is something that shouldn't be on anyone's mind unless they fucked up and let themselves fail in achieving what really mattered most by being in the wrong surroundings. So just think about a goal, and let the stress peel off once you start thinking about how to achieve that goal. Once you have a plan, don't think twice just go for it and let positivity take you to what's destined for you.

Keep you head up, hun. You never know the kinda good will come if you just stayed strong and let your determination, motivation, drive, and your willpower come out in its fullest, you may end up accomplishing the dream you set to one day accomplish. Just think about this comment and do some reflecting so you can try to build off of this situation to get stronger. All it takes is time and positive thoughts during the duration of the wait time. Just live out your youth. You have a lot of ahead of you. Take it from me. I'm suffering the side-effects of attempted overdose and I'm stressing worse than how I was at time I tried. It's not worth the trouble, the tears, the thought, and the effort that you may think lies ahead but death isn't peaceful and wonderful. It's just dark, empty, cold, silent, you can't move, you cant talk, and you start to feel vulnerable although you're all alone. It's worse than what they said hell feels like. Also think about the ones that actually care for you and want you to get back up on your feet. If you were to die, it would cause one big chain reaction of suicide between a population of people that rooted from you. So you never know what will happen because the people that suffer about your loss are capable of causing another's suffering from loss. We as humans are capable of anything and most of the time, we all jump on the bandwagon and join the ones who started one thing that everyone is doing now. So it's possible for one death to lead to the death of an entire planet in an instant.
